issues.legal_issue: An order granting a temporary injunction, including an ex parte order, may be challenged either before the court that made it or by appeal where the Code provides an appeal.
material_facts: The plaintiff obtained an ex parte temporary injunction restraining the defendants from evicting him except through due process of law.
The defendants challenged the order in the High Court instead of first seeking relief from the trial court or pursuing the statutory appeal.
issues.conclusion: An affected party may choose either to approach the court that passed the ex parte order for relief or to appeal against it.
issues.legal_principle: Section 104 and Order 43 Rule 1(r) of the Code of Civil Procedure provide for an appeal from an order under Order 39 Rules 1, 2, 2A, 4 or 10. Order 39 Rule 1 is the source of the power to grant temporary injunctions with or without notice, and an order made under that power is appealable. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.temporary_injunction_proceeding: The proceeding concerns an application for a temporary injunction.
predicates.injunction_order_made: The court made an order granting a temporary injunction.
predicates.party_affected_by_order: A party is affected by the injunction order.

issues.definition: When a temporary-injunction order affects a party, that party may seek relief from the court that made the order or by appeal.

issues.legal_issue: A beneficiary of an ex parte injunction who fails to perform the required service and filing duties cannot take advantage of the order when the other party does not obey it.
material_facts: The trial court granted an ex parte injunction and directed compliance with Order 39 Rule 3.
The Court considered the consequences if the party obtaining such an order fails to perform the duties required when an injunction is granted without notice.
issues.conclusion: A beneficiary who fails to comply with the duties required for an ex parte injunction cannot take advantage of the order if the other party disobeys it, and cannot complain of that disobedience.
issues.legal_principle: Order 39 Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires reasons for granting an injunction without notice and requires the applicant to deliver or send specified documents to the opposite party and file an affidavit confirming that step. The order may be understood to contain those requirements by implication, but failure by its beneficiary to perform the duties has consequences. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.ex_parte_injunction_granted: The court grants an injunction without first giving notice to the opposing party.
predicates.beneficiary_fails_required_service_or_fi: The party obtaining the injunction fails to provide the required documents or file the required confirmation.
predicates.opposing_party_disobeys_order: The opposing party does not obey the injunction.

issues.definition: If an ex parte injunction beneficiary fails to complete the required service or filing and the opposing party disobeys the order, the beneficiary cannot take advantage of it or complain of that disobedience.

issues.legal_issue: An ex parte injunction does not become illegal merely because its stated duration exceeds the period within which the application should be finally decided.
material_facts: The trial court granted an ex parte injunction until further orders.
The High Court considered the injunction impermissible because it could operate beyond thirty days.
issues.conclusion: The order does not become illegal merely because it was not limited to thirty days or less.
issues.legal_principle: Order 39 Rule 3A of the Code of Civil Procedure requires the court to endeavour to finally dispose of an application for an ex parte injunction within thirty days and to record reasons if unable to do so. It does not require the injunction itself to be limited to thirty days. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.ex_parte_injunction_granted: The court grants an injunction without first giving notice to the opposing party.
predicates.order_continues_until_further_order: The injunction is expressed to continue until a further order rather than ending within the initial period for deciding the application.

issues.definition: An ex parte injunction expressed to continue until further order is not illegal solely because it lasts beyond the period for initially deciding the injunction application.

issues.legal_issue: When the court fails to comply with the requirements for timely consideration of an ex parte injunction, an aggrieved party may appeal against the continuing order while the injunction application remains pending.
material_facts: Order 39 Rule 3A required timely consideration of an application for an injunction granted without notice and written reasons if the court could not decide it within the prescribed period.

The Court held that an aggrieved party should not have to bear the consequences of the court’s failure to follow that mandate and that the failure to decide the application could be treated as a final order for appeal purposes.
issues.conclusion: Where the mandate of Order 39 Rule 3A is flouted, the aggrieved party is entitled to appeal against the order that remains in force despite the pending application; the appellate court must entertain the appeal and take account of the omission. For appeal purposes, failure to decide the application or vacate the injunction is deemed a final order on expiry of the period specified in the Rule.
issues.legal_principle: Order 39 Rule 3A of the Code of Civil Procedure requires the court to endeavour to decide an ex parte injunction application within thirty days and to record reasons if it cannot do so. Order 43 Rule 1 provides the usual appeal from specified injunction orders. Where the court fails to meet the Rule 3A mandate, the continuing order is treated as a final order for purposes of an appeal, so the affected party is not left without a remedy. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.ex_parte_injunction_proceeding: The proceeding concerns an injunction granted without notice to the opposing party.
predicates.application_remains_undecided_beyond_req: The court has not finally decided the injunction application within the required period.
predicates.court_fails_to_record_reasons_for_inabil: The court does not record reasons for being unable to decide the application within the required period.
predicates.affected_party_seeks_appeal: A party affected by the continuing injunction seeks to appeal.

issues.definition: If an ex parte injunction application remains undecided beyond the required period without recorded reasons and an affected party appeals, that party may appeal against the continuing order as if it were final.

issues.legal_issue: A High Court should ordinarily direct a party challenging an interim ex parte injunction to use available remedies before invoking its constitutional supervisory jurisdiction.
material_facts: The defendants challenged the trial court’s ex parte injunction under Article 227 of the Constitution.
They could have applied to the trial court to vacate or modify the order or appealed against it.
The High Court entertained the petition, although the Supreme Court observed that it need not have done so.
issues.conclusion: The High Court should not have entertained the petition in the first instance and should have directed the affected party to pursue one of the alternative remedies, though constitutional powers themselves cannot be restricted by a bar against their exercise.
issues.legal_principle: Article 227 of the Constitution confers supervisory power, but the recognized principle is that the High Court should ordinarily direct a party to use available alternative remedies before resorting to a constitutional remedy. In this setting, the available remedies were an application to the court that made the order and an appeal under Section 104 and Order 43 Rule 1(r) of the Code of Civil Procedure. No earlier cases are relied on.

predicates.constitutional_supervisory_proceeding: A party invokes the High Court’s constitutional supervisory jurisdiction.
predicates.interim_injunction_challenged: The proceeding challenges an interim injunction order.
predicates.adequate_alternative_remedies_available: The affected party can seek relief from the court that made the order or pursue an appeal.

issues.definition: When a party challenges an interim injunction through constitutional supervision despite having alternative remedies, the High Court should ordinarily direct the party to use one of those remedies.

issues.legal_issue: The parties must maintain the status quo that existed immediately before the suit until the trial court finally decides the pending injunction application.
material_facts: The High Court directed the trial court to decide the plaintiff’s interlocutory injunction application on its merits and in accordance with law.
The Supreme Court directed that the parties maintain the status quo that existed immediately before the suit until the trial court made that decision.
issues.conclusion: The parties must maintain the status quo as it existed immediately before the suit until the trial court passes final orders on the injunction application.
issues.legal_principle: The Court issued this direction to govern the parties’ conduct pending the trial court’s decision on the interlocutory injunction application. No specific statutory provision or earlier case is relied on for this direction.

predicates.temporary_injunction_proceeding: The proceeding concerns an application for a temporary injunction.
predicates.injunction_application_pending_final_dec: The trial court has not yet finally decided the injunction application.
predicates.pre_suit_status_quo_identifiable: The circumstances existing immediately before the suit can be identified.

issues.definition: While the injunction application remains undecided, the parties must preserve the identifiable status quo that existed immediately before the suit.
